allowable_load.basis: structural load Q_DL+LL = q_all,net x A' = (q_ult/FS - q) x A', A' = B'L' the effective area, the foundation and the soil over it taken at the soil's unit weight (UFC 3-220-20 Sec. 5-2.2 Eq. 5-3, p. 276; Sec. 5-2.4 Eq. 5-14, p. 279); under an eccentric load, q_all x A' - q x A, the load on A' (Eq. 5-10, p. 277) and the foundation's and the soil's weight on the whole footing A. gross load = q_all x A' = Q_DL+LL + W_F + W_S, the total load on the bearing surface with the foundation's and the overlying soil's weight in it (Eq. 5-1, p. 275), so it is not the structural load. GEC-6 Sec. 5.2.2 (p. 53) recommends the allowable bearing capacity on the gross pressure, the self-weight of the footing and the backfill over it counted in the applied load; a footing heavier than the soil it replaces leaves less for the column (GEC-6 Sec. 6.3.1, p. 113)

result.neutral_plane_basis: UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 procedure: the neutral plane is where the load curve (Q_dead + negative skin friction) meets the resistance curve (toe resistance + positive skin friction), with side and base resistance fully mobilized (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 steps 3-5, Fig 6-26). Unit skin friction (beta layers) and the toe in sand use the final effective stress, sigma'v0 plus the fill / drawdown change (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2). The pile's own weight is left out of the load curve, as UFC 3-220-20 Fig 6-26 and FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 do (include_pile_weight=False).
result.methods_range: The methods give neutral planes from 5.99 m to 17.66 m and drag forces from 226 kN to 1308 kN (5 of 7 methods apply).
warnings: The neutral plane where the load and resistance curves intersect (17.66 m) lies below 5.99 m, where the computed soil settlement falls to the pile's; the friction between them is counted as negative although that soil settles less than the pile. With full mobilization that is UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4's conservative assumption for the drag force. For settlement, full base mobilization is not conservative (§6-5.8.4.2): see the 50% and 0% toe mobilization rows (toe_mobilization).

The soil below the pile toe has no compressibility in this model (18.00-20.00 m (cohesionless)), so its settlement counts as zero (here 0.0 mm below the toe in all). The toe load counts down to 18.86 m, where its stress increase falls below 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, p. 449): extend the profile at least that deep. The fill / drawdown stress increase does not decay with depth: give the profile down to the base of the compressible soil. Give Cc and e0 (or C_ec) for clay, or E_s for sand, to include it, and mark a layer settling if the fill / drawdown compresses it (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs 6-49 to 6-54, the equivalent footing at the toe).

FHWA GEC-12 Vol I §7.3.5.6 step 1c (p. 332) takes the settlement below the toe to 25.70 m, below the bottom of the soil profile (20.00 m), so the UFC 3-220-20 and FHWA GEC-12 depths were compared only to the bottom of the profile: pile head settlement 0.7 mm by UFC 3-220-20's and at least 0.7 mm by FHWA GEC-12's. Give the soil profile down to 25.70 m to compare them.

neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Intersection of the load and resistance curves, side fully mobilized, toe at 50% of its nominal resistance: UFC §6-5.8.4.2 and GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 analyse 0%, 50% and 100% (Siegel et al. 2013).

neutral_plane_comparison.name: Mobilized toe resistance compatible with the toe penetration
neutral_plane_comparison.assumptions: Pile and soil settle equally at the neutral plane (Fig 6-19). The toe force follows the toe penetration: bearing-stratum compression under the toe force (UFC Eqs 6-51 to 6-54) standing in for a q-z curve, capped at the toe resistance; side fully mobilized.

neutral_plane_comparison.source: FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.7 (p. 336; Goudreault and Fellenius 1994); CGPR #56 Table 3.1 'end bearing'

below_toe.basis: Below the toe (18.00 m) the toe force (1665.2 kN) is spread 2V:1H from an equivalent footing 0.40 m square at the toe (UFC 3-220-20 Eqs 6-49 to 6-52) and counted 0.86 m below the toe, to 18.86 m, where its stress increase falls below 10% of the bearing stress of the equivalent footing (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.8.4.3, p. 449). The fill / drawdown stress increase does not decay with depth, but no layer between the toe and the bottom of the soil profile (20.00 m) is marked settling, so it adds no settlement there. With 10% of the existing vertical effective stress instead (FHWA GEC-12 §7.3.5.6 step 1c, p. 332; influence_depth_criterion='effective_stress') the toe force is counted to the bottom of the soil profile, 20.00 m, short of 25.70 m, where its stress increase would fall below that: the same settlement below the toe, 0.0 mm.

The ultimate toe resistance, qb = Nq sigma'zD (UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-20; GEC-12 Eq. 7-20 with Table 7-9 for its beta method, p. 258), sigma'v final (skin_friction_stress); the drag procedures leave the method to the engineer (UFC §6-7.4 step 2; GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 Step 2). Table 6-17's Fellenius (2021) column, like GEC-12 Table 7-9 (p. 256), prints only each soil type's Nt range beside its phi' range (sand: Nt 30 to 150 over phi' 32 to 40 deg); the straight line in phi' between the ends, and a phi' outside the range held at its end, is this module's reading, not printed. UFC §6-7.4 step 2's advice on lower and higher values is for side friction (alpha and beta); for the toe, neutral_plane_comparison gives the neutral plane at 0 %, 50 % and 100 % of the toe resistance.
alternatives: Nt 39.0 (UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-17, p. 421, Cheng (2004) equation; phi' 34 deg, Z/b 45.0): Nt_method 'cheng'
Nt 30, the sand range's low end in Table 6-17 (phi' 32 deg): give Nt 30
Nt 150, the sand range's high end in Table 6-17 (phi' 40 deg): give Nt 150
Nt given: local experience (GEC-12 Step 5a) or a mobilized value

choices.what: skin friction method in the cohesive soil, 0-6 m
choices.chosen: Alpha method, fs = alpha x cu (UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-8)
choices.basis: The module's default for cohesive soil: undrained, short-term conditions (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.4.2, p. 414, and p. 410), as in UFC's drag force example (App. B-5.4, p. 636); FHWA recommends the α-method in cohesive soils (GEC-12 §7.2.1.2, p. 229). Either serves the drag procedures: 'an appropriate static analysis method' (GEC-12 §7.3.6.1 Step 2, p. 342); higher alpha and beta are conservative for negative skin friction (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2, p. 476).
alternatives: Beta method, fs = beta x sigma'v (UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-7), for long-term, drained conditions (UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.4.1, p. 411; FHWA GEC-12 §7.2.1.3.4, p. 255): skin_friction_method 'beta' with beta (GEC-12 Table 7-9, p. 256: clay 0.15-0.35)

choices.what: beta in the cohesionless soil, 6-18 m
choices.basis: The module's default, by soil_class (sand unless given). GEC-12 Table 7-9 (p. 256; Step 2b, p. 257) prints only each soil type's range of phi', beta and Nt; UFC 3-220-20 Table 6-15 (p. 414) pairs beta's ends with phi' for driven piles (sand: beta 0.30 at phi' 32 deg, 0.90 at 40 deg). The straight line in phi' between the ends, and a phi' outside the range held at its end, is this module's reading; neither manual prints it. UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2 (p. 476): lower alpha and beta are conservative for resistance, higher alpha and beta for negative skin friction.
alternatives: beta 0.30, the sand range's low end in Table 6-15 (phi' 32 deg), conservative for resistance: give the layer beta 0.30
beta 0.90, the sand range's high end in Table 6-15 (phi' 40 deg), conservative for negative skin friction: give the layer beta 0.90
beta given: local experience (GEC-12 Step 2a), or UFC 3-220-20 Eq 6-6, K tan delta (Fig 6-13, Table 6-14)
soil_class 'silt' or 'gravel'

choices.what: alpha in the cohesive soil, 0-6 m
choices.basis: The module's default, as the module follows UFC 3-220-20's procedure by default. UFC 3-220-20 §6-5.4.2 (pp. 415-417): alpha 1 in soft clay (su below 800 psf, Table 6-16); in firm to very stiff clay Fig 6-14, curve A for Z of 40b or more and curve B for Z = 10b, Z from the ground surface to the clay's base or the pile toe and b the pile width. UFC's drag example reads it so (App. B-5.4, pp. 636-637: alpha 1.0 in soft clay, 0.5 in stiff clay, Eq 6-9 in the transition zone).
alternatives: FHWA GEC-12 Fig. 7-17 (Tomlinson 1979): alpha_chart 'gec12_fig_7_17' with fig_7_17_curve; Ca by su, D/b and pile type, as drawn (GEC-12 §7.2.1.3.2 Step 1, p. 250)
alpha given on the layer; a higher alpha is conservative for negative skin friction, a lower one for resistance (UFC 3-220-20 §6-7.4 step 2, p. 476)

notes: Pressure above the excavation: sand apparent envelope (max 31.20 kPa) + surcharge 4.00 kPa (GEC-4 5.2.4 adds surcharge and water explicitly).
The bottom span's load is assigned wholly to the lowest support; free earth support gives that support 72.7 kN/m from the wall below it.
Embedment: free earth support about the lowest support, MR = FS x MD with FS = 1.5 (Caltrans T&S 8-4 uses 1.3).

choices.basis: The Caltrans Trenching and Shoring Manual, which these solvers follow (Secs. 7-5.02 and 8-4.02), takes Rankine's where its examples have no wall friction: 'since the wall friction (delta) is zero, use Rankine earth pressure theory to calculate the active and passive earth pressure coefficients' (pp. 7-18, 7-27 and 9-12), each time with the note 'Rankine theory tends to underestimate the passive earth pressure. It is recommended to use the Log-Spiral model to compute the passive earth force' (p. 7-27; 'Log-Spiral-Rankine Model', pp. 7-18 and 9-13); Example 8-1 takes the log-spiral Kp at delta 15 deg on phi 30 deg (p. 8-12); and Sec. 4-6 (p. 4-28) says Rankine's theory 'should not be used to calculate the passive earth pressure forces for a shoring system because it does not account for wall friction'. The module keeps Rankine's, the smaller Kp, as its default; passive_theory 'log_spiral' takes the log-spiral Kp with wall friction. At delta = 0 the two are the same Kp
alternatives: log_spiral (passive_theory 'log_spiral'), UFC 3-220-20 Eq. 4-12, with passive_wall_friction_deg left out: delta/phi' 0.66, none with cohesion: layer 1: Kp 3; embedment 2.99 m

result.verdict: FAILS: sliding (FOS 1.17 < 1.50 required). Passes: overturning (FOS 2.67 >= 2.00 required); bearing (q_max 200.1 kPa <= q_allowable 250.0 kPa, FOS 1.25); eccentricity (resultant within the middle third: e = 0.580 m <= B/6 = 0.600 m).

choices.chosen: 21.3 deg = 2/3 phi_f, phi_f = 32 deg, the foundation soil's friction angle (phi_foundation)
choices.basis: a base not cast against the ground: EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(10) (p. 64) takes 2/3 phi'cv;d for smooth precast foundations; UFC 3-220-20 Fig. 4-27 (p. 220) takes tan delta, the friction factor between soil and base, from Table 4-1 (p. 184), e.g. mass concrete on clean fine to medium sand 24-29 deg
alternatives: phi_f = 32 deg (delta_base = 32): concrete cast against the ground: GEC-6 Sec. 5.4 (p. 99): 'For concrete cast against cohesionless or granular material, the coefficient of friction, tan delta, will be equal to the tangent of the friction angle (tan phi) for the soil supporting the footing'; EN 1997-1 Sec. 6.5.3(10) (p. 64): phi'cv;d for cast-in-situ concrete foundations

choices.what: live-load surcharge over the heel, in sliding, overturning and the eccentricity check
choices.basis: FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.5 (p. 10-43): 'the live load surcharge is not considered as a stabilizing force over the heel of the wall when sliding resistance is being checked'; Sec. 10.5.3 (p. 10-41): for CIP semi-gravity walls the surcharge loads are 'conservatively neglected within the width of the base slab since they contribute to overturning and sliding resistance'; UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.2 (p. 597): 'For overturning and sliding checks, it is assumed that the traffic pressure does not act over the wall heel'; GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-22 (AASHTO): external loads that increase sliding resistance are included 'only if those loads are permanent', so the vertical component of the live load's thrust is left out too
alternatives: counted as a resisting force (live_load_resists=True): counted: the free body with the live load over the heel whenever it acts behind the wall (the module's reading before GM-157); none of the references above counts a live load so

choices.what: pavement or slab over the backfill
choices.chosen: modelled as retained soil up to the ground surface; a surcharge is transient live load (its thrust counts in every check, its weight over the heel does not resist sliding or overturning)
choices.basis: the usual practice for pavements and slabs; dead_load_resists=true counts a dead-load surcharge over the heel as resisting weight in sliding and overturning

choices.what: surcharge over the heel, in the bearing pressures
choices.basis: UFC 3-220-20 App. B-1.6 (p. 602): 'Unlike the checks of overturning and sliding, it is conservative to include the surcharge over the heel of the wall, if this is possible to occur, in the bearing capacity check'; GEC-11 Vol I p. 4-26: 'the bearing check applies live load above both the reinforced zone and the retained backfill'
alternatives: left out (surcharge_in_bearing=False): left out of the base pressures, the surcharge taken as located behind the heel (FHWA NHI-06-089 Sec. 10.5.3, p. 10-41)

choices.basis: m_alpha = cos(a) (1 + tan(a) tan(phi) / F), at the method's own F, is the denominator of the normal force on a slice base; below 0.2 the factor of safety may be incorrect or misleading (Whitman & Bailey 1967), and Slide2 reports such a surface as invalid with its 'Check malpha < 0.2' setting on (its error -112), circular or not; slices with phi' = 0 are not checked: there m_alpha = cos(a) does not depend on F and the shear strength is c l whatever the normal force, so leaving such a surface out would only raise the minimum; on 25 slices the governing surface's FOS is 1.583 and its least m_alpha 0.80; on 50 slices, 1.583 and 0.79
